title: Kabaddi: overview

The sport is governed by official laws that cover the field of play, equipment, players, officials, scoring, fouls, and conduct; this database walks through every one of those areas so a newcomer can follow a full match with understanding.

title: The objective
d: The objective of Kabaddi is: outscore the opponent with raid points.
definition: The objective of Kabaddi is: outscore the opponent with raid points.
description: Every rule in Kabaddi exists to serve one objective: outscore the opponent with raid points. All tactics, positions, and scoring flow from that single aim. Beginners should fix the objective in mind first, because every foul, stoppage, and strategy in the sport is judged against whether it fairly advances or unfairly blocks that objective. Coaches return to it constantly: if a play does not serve the objective, it is the wrong play.

title: How games are won

definition: Kabaddi: 1 point per tagged defender; defenders score for stopping the raider; most points wins.

Because of that, late-game strategy everywhere in the sport is clock-and-score management — protecting a lead or chasing one changes every decision, from how much risk to take to when to slow play down or speed it up. title: Ties and tiebreakers
d: Tied games in Kabaddi are resolved under the competition rules for the level of play.
definition: Tied games in Kabaddi are resolved under the competition rules for the level of play.
description: Not every contest in Kabaddi can end tied: league games may allow draws while knockout games must produce a winner through extra time, tiebreak procedures, or shootouts defined by the competition. Tiebreak rules are announced before play and never invented mid-game; players and coaches must know them, because they reshape tactics — a team may play for penalties, or gamble everything to avoid them.

title: Match duration
d: Kabaddi contests last: two 20-minute halves.
definition: Kabaddi contests last: two 20-minute halves.
description: A Kabaddi contest runs two 20-minute halves. Duration shapes fitness demands: athletes train to be sharp in the final stretch, not just the first. Timekeeping is an official duty — the clock, not the players, decides when it ends, and added or extra time exists to compensate for stoppages so the advertised duration is genuinely played.

title: Periods and breaks
d: Play in Kabaddi is divided into periods with breaks as defined for the competition.
definition: Play in Kabaddi is divided into periods with breaks as defined for the competition.
description: The two 20-minute halves in Kabaddi give coaches their main lever: adjustments, substitutions, and rest happen in the breaks. Teams plan for three phases — start fast, manage the middle, finish strong — and the side that uses its breaks better often wins the second half. Break length and number are fixed by the rules; exceeding them can draw penalties.

definition: Kabaddi surfaces must be safe, level, and marked to regulation.
description: The playing surface in Kabaddi must be safe, level, and marked to regulation. Surface changes tactics: fast surfaces reward speed and quick passing, slow or soft ones reward power and patience. Footwear and equipment rules usually assume a specific surface, and playing on the wrong one risks both injury and disqualification of the contest.

Beginners should buy for safety and fit first, performance second; the right size matters more than the brand.

title: The ball

definition: The Kabaddi ball is specified by the laws: size, weight, and pressure are regulated.

Ball specs change the whole game — a lighter, livelier ball rewards touch, a heavier one rewards power. Match balls are approved and often supplied by the competition; warming up with the wrong spec builds the wrong feel.

definition: Protection in Kabaddi: required and recommended gear keeps players safe within the laws.
description: Protection is part of the laws of Kabaddi, not an afterthought. Required and recommended gear exists because the sport's known injury patterns are known: the rules mandate the gear that prevents the common ones. Gear must fit and be worn correctly — loose or missing protection can keep a player off the field, and no contest is worth a preventable injury.

title: Team size
d: Kabaddi is played 7 per side.
definition: Kabaddi is played 7 per side.
description: Kabaddi is played 7 per side. Numbers decide the geometry of the game: more players means more structure and specialization, fewer means more space and versatility. Every player must know the legal team size, because playing short — or with too many — brings penalties, and planned rotations are built around the allowed numbers.

title: Positions and roles
d: Positions in Kabaddi divide the work: each role has a zone, duties, and skills.
definition: Positions in Kabaddi divide the work: each role has a zone, duties, and skills.
description: Positions in Kabaddi exist to divide the 7 per side into manageable jobs. Each role has a home zone, primary duties, and a skill profile; great teams are built by fitting people to roles, not roles to people. Beginners should learn one position deeply before roaming — mastery of a role teaches the whole game faster than playing everywhere badly.

title: Substitutions
d: Substitution rules in Kabaddi control how and when players may be replaced.
definition: Substitution rules in Kabaddi control how and when players may be replaced.
description: Substitutions in Kabaddi are a tactical weapon governed by strict procedure: only at stoppages, only through the official, only within the allowed number. Coaches plan substitution windows the way generals plan reserves — fresh legs at the right moment win tight games. Illegal substitution procedure can cost a team a player or a penalty.

title: Officials

definition: Kabaddi is officiated by: referee, umpires, scorer.
description: Kabaddi is officiated by referee, umpires, scorer. Officials are neutral arbiters of the laws: their decisions on matters of fact are final during play, and dissent is penalized. Knowing what each official watches helps players stay legal — most fouls are committed in full view of exactly the official assigned to that zone.

title: The referee's role
d: The referee in Kabaddi enforces the laws, keeps time, and manages conduct.
definition: The referee in Kabaddi enforces the laws, keeps time, and manages conduct.
description: The referee's job in Kabaddi is bigger than blowing a whistle: enforcing the laws, keeping time, managing conduct, and protecting player safety — in that order. Players may ask for clarification respectfully; they may not dispute decisions. At every level, the referee's authority begins when they enter the venue and ends when they leave it.

title: Fouls
d: Illegal play in Kabaddi draws fouls under the laws; persistent fouling draws cards or ejections.
definition: Illegal play in Kabaddi draws fouls under the laws; persistent fouling draws cards or ejections.
description: A foul in Kabaddi is illegal play as defined by the laws — not just rough play, but any act the rules forbid. Officials grade fouls by intent, danger, and advantage gained; persistent or cynical fouling draws escalating punishment. Smart players learn the exact line: physical right up to it, never across it.

title: Penalties
d: Fouls in Kabaddi are punished by free plays, spot penalties, or loss of possession per the laws.
definition: Fouls in Kabaddi are punished by free plays, spot penalties, or loss of possession per the laws.
description: Punishment in Kabaddi fits the foul: minor infringements restart play for the other side, serious ones award direct scoring chances or remove the offender. Penalty rules are deliberately severe enough that fouling is never a good trade — the team that stays disciplined keeps eleven (or its equivalent) on the field and wins the close ones.

title: Discipline and conduct
d: Misconduct in Kabaddi — dissent, dangerous play, unsporting behavior — is penalized, up to ejection.
definition: Misconduct in Kabaddi — dissent, dangerous play, unsporting behavior — is penalized, up to ejection.
description: The laws of Kabaddi punish misconduct on a ladder: warnings, cards, sin-bins, ejections, suspensions. Dissent, dangerous play, and unsporting behavior are treated as seriously as technical fouls, because the game depends on respect for officials and opponents. Captains are responsible for their team's conduct and speak to the referee for the side.

title: Basic strategy

definition: Kabaddi strategy starts from the objective: outscore the opponent with raid points.
description: All Kabaddi strategy serves the objective: outscore the opponent with raid points. The basic game plan is simple — win your individual battles, keep your shape, and take the chances the scoring system rewards most. Beginners win by doing simple things reliably; advanced players win by forcing opponents into mistakes while making none themselves.

title: Offense
d: Attacking in Kabaddi means creating the scoring chances the rules reward.
definition: Attacking in Kabaddi means creating the scoring chances the rules reward.
description: Attacking Kabaddi is about manufacturing the highest-percentage chances the scoring system allows. Good offense is patient until the opening appears, then ruthless: create space, move the defense, and finish. The best attacks look simple because every player knows the plan two passes ahead.

title: Defense

definition: Defending in Kabaddi means denying the objective: outscore the opponent with raid points.
description: Defending Kabaddi starts from denying the objective: outscore the opponent with raid points. Good defense is organized first and aggressive second — shape, communication, and patience, with pressure applied where the opponent is weakest. The great defensive teams all share one trait: every player defends, all the time, without being asked.

Those first written laws are the ancestor of every rule in this database — the game you watch today is their descendant.

definition: Modern Kabaddi: professional leagues, world championships, and Olympic or global stages.
description: Modern Kabaddi grew through professional leagues, world championships, and global competition. Television and professionalism standardized the laws worldwide and turned the best players into full-time athletes. The modern game is faster, stronger, and more tactical than any earlier era — but it is played under the same essential objective the founders wrote down.

title: Variations

definition: Kabaddi has official and informal variations with adjusted rules for numbers, space, and level.
description: Every major sport spawns variations: small-sided, beach, indoor, youth, and disability versions of Kabaddi all adjust numbers, space, and rules while keeping the soul of the game. Variations are where most people actually play — the full eleven-a-side (or equivalent) version is the tip of a much bigger pyramid.

title: Safety
d: Play Kabaddi safely: warm up, wear the required gear, follow the foul laws, and stop for injury.
definition: Play Kabaddi safely: warm up, wear the required gear, follow the foul laws, and stop for injury.
description: Safety in Kabaddi is part of the rules, not separate from them: warm up properly, wear every required piece of gear, respect the foul laws that exist to prevent injury, and stop play for any head injury or suspected serious harm. No game, drill, or tryout is worth playing hurt — the laws protect players who protect themselves.
